title: Custom EventEmitter with 'once' and Unsubscribe
subtopicTitle: DOM Event Flow: Capturing, Bubbling & Delegation
problemStatement: Implement `EventEmitter` with methods: `on(event, listener)`, `emit(event, ...args)`, `off(event, listener)`, and `once(event, listener)`. `on()` and `once()` must return an unsubscribe function `() => void`.
interviewTrap: Modifying the listeners array/set while iterating over it during `emit` causes subsequent listeners to be skipped. Always iterate over a snapshot copy.

testCases.name: Notifies listeners upon emit with parameters
testCases.testFn: const ee = new EventEmitter(); const log = []; ee.on('data', x => log.push(x)); ee.emit('data', 'val'); return log;

testCases.name: once() fires exactly one time then unregisters
testCases.testFn: const ee = new EventEmitter(); let count = 0; ee.once('ping', () => count++); ee.emit('ping'); ee.emit('ping'); return count;

testCases.name: Returned unsubscribe function removes listener
testCases.testFn: const ee = new EventEmitter(); let count = 0; const unsub = ee.on('tick', () => count++); ee.emit('tick'); unsub(); ee.emit('tick'); return count;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Events travel down from `window` through the DOM tree (Capturing Phase) until they reach the target (Target Phase), then bubble back up to `window` (Bubbling Phase). Event delegation attaches a single listener to a common ancestor, querying `event.target.closest()`.

2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
